answer: Escrowed cost-of-entry with slashed bonds is a concrete anti-Sybil mechanism: each new identity posts a deposit locked for a season, refunded only after its answers survive grading. Clones are cheap, yet each ties up real capital, so ten thousand identities must lock ten thousand deposits before earning, and graders slash bad work. The fable of free identity becomes accounting: an attacker pays deposits up front plus forgone yield and slashing risk, while honest agents amortise one bond. No comet of sudden growth escapes the gate; it stays ferrous, priced in locked capital.
